GeneticProgramming.description: Watch 3D creatures evolve generation by generation toward a fitness goal no individual understands. Population grid displays organisms with fitness labels. Auto-evolve ticks on a timer or step manually. Creatures converge on similar body plans despite random initialization — convergent evolution from pure math. Evolution does not design — it accumulates accidents that happen to survive.
GeneticProgramming.qfep_connection: phi-dE — the rate of evolutionary change. Each generation is a dE step. Fitness is the selection pressure (phi) that amplifies some mutations and kills others. Lambda emerges as the mutation rate: too low and evolution stalls, too high and it melts.
GeneticProgramming.gamwell_reference: Constraint satisfaction, evolutionary computation, genetic algorithms
GeneticProgramming.capacity: WATCH evolution accumulate accidents that happen to survive — design without a designer
interactions: observe fitness labels on population grid
GeneticProgramming.name: GeneticProgramming

crackpropagation_ca.description: A cellular automaton that grows fracture networks from invisible stress. A 64x64 grid accumulates stress through diffusion and decay — when a cell crosses the crack threshold, it shatters and pushes stress outward. The result is realistic branching cracks that follow paths of least resistance, guided by direction bias that prevents zig-zag. You watch destruction emerge from accumulation: nothing visible happens until the threshold breaks, then cracks bloom explosively across the surface.
crackpropagation_ca.name: crackpropagation_ca
crackpropagation_ca.qfep_connection: Edge of chaos — the crack threshold is the critical lambda where order (intact material) meets entropy (shattered field). Below threshold: stability. Above: catastrophic branching. The propagation rate tunes how fast the phase transition sweeps through the grid.
crackpropagation_ca.gamwell_reference: Fracture mechanics, cellular automata, stress propagation, percolation theory, crack branching patterns in nature
interactions: watch cracks emerge from the center stress seed
observe branching patterns following direction bias
notice how crack width varies with local stress intensity
compare dense shatter (low threshold) vs sparse fractures (high threshold)
crackpropagation_ca.capacity: PREDICT how cellular automaton crack propagation creates realistic fracture networks from local stress transfer and threshold-based state transitions.

mushrooms.description: A procedural mushroom meadow grown from noise. FastNoiseLite drives a spatial Poisson process — mushrooms spawn where noise exceeds a density threshold, creating natural clearings and clusters. Five species templates produce variety; a glowing variant adds bioluminescent accents. Fairy rings self-organize as perfect circles of identical species within the random field. The ground itself is procedurally deformed, and ambient lighting creates a forest-floor atmosphere. Walk through and feel how randomness filtered through ecological rules produces something that looks alive.
mushrooms.name: Mushrooms
mushrooms.qfep_connection: E(S) entropy filtered through ecological form — noise is the raw entropy, density threshold is the filter, and species templates are the forms that entropy fills. Fairy rings are emergent order: lambda-tuning where structured patterns crystallize from random placement.
mushrooms.gamwell_reference: Spatial Poisson processes, noise-driven procedural generation, fairy ring mycology, bioluminescent fungi, ecological niche theory
interactions: find fairy rings — perfect circles of identical species
spot glowing mushrooms in the undergrowth
notice how clearings form from noise thresholds
mushrooms.capacity: EXPLAIN how noise-driven spatial processes create naturalistic distributions and how fairy rings emerge as self-organized order within random fields.

tree_gen.description: An infinite procedural forest that grows around you. Trees spawn within a generation radius as you walk, and vanish behind you when you leave. The generation loop is the algorithm: proximity check, spacing constraint, spawn, cull. No tree exists until you approach; the forest is an illusion maintained by continuous generation. Two tree styles (simple blocks and complex clusters) with red emissive materials create an alien forest that feels both procedural and alive.
tree_gen.name: Tree Generator
tree_gen.qfep_connection: Pure phi — the rate of change IS the content. The forest exists only as a process of generation and removal. Stop walking and the forest freezes. The generation_distance parameter controls how far ahead reality extends.
tree_gen.gamwell_reference: Procedural world generation, infinite terrain, proximity-based LOD, parametric tree generation, spatial hashing
interactions: walk forward to generate new trees ahead
look behind to see trees vanishing at removal distance
observe two tree styles appearing randomly
tree_gen.capacity: BUILD a proximity-based procedural spawning system that creates and destroys content around the player position to simulate infinite generated worlds.
